'''Suhas Pandurang Sukhatme''' is an Indian scientist, teacher, author and a former chairman of the [[Atomic Energy Regulatory Board]] of the Government of India, known for his expertise in [[heat transfer]] and energy technologies.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle">{{cite web | url=http://www.itbhuglobal.org/chronicle/archives/2008/10/index-interviews.php | title=ITBHU Chronicle | publisher=ITBHU Chronicle |year=2014 | access-date=10 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="INSA">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=N95-1194 | title=INSA | publisher=INSA |year=2014 | access-date=10 January 2015 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://archive.today/20150117084920/http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=N95-1194 | archive-date=17 January 2015 }}</ref><ref name="Interview">{{cite interview | title=Interview with Prof. (Padmashree) S. P Sukhatme | date=28 October 2008 | access-date=10 January 2015 | last=S. P Sukhatme | interviewer=Chronicle Editor – Indian Institute of Technology, Banres Hindu University | url=http://www.itbhuglobal.org/chronicle/archives/2008/10/index-interviews.php}}</ref><ref name="IITGn">{{cite web | url=http://www.iitgn.ac.in/aac/administration_aac_prof_suhas.html | title=IITGn | publisher=IITGn |year=2014 | access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref> He was honoured by the [[Government of India]], in 2001, with the fourth highest [[Indian honours system|Indian civilian award]] of [[Padma Shri]].<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web | url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | title=Padma Awards | publisher=Padma Awards |year=2014 | access-date=11 November 2014}}</ref>

==Biography==
Suhas Pandurang Sukhatme was born to Indumati Sukhatme and [[Pandurang Vasudeo Sukhatme]], renowned statistician and a [[Padma Bhushan]] award winner, on 5 November 1938<ref name="INSA" /> at [[Baroda]] in the Western Indian state of [[Maharashtra]].<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /> He graduated in Engineering in 1958 from the [[Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi]] and pursued his higher studies at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. He secured a master's degree (SM) in 1960, a higher degree in Engineering (MechE) in 1961, and a doctoral degree (ScD) in 1964.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IITGn" />

During his stay at MIT, he worked as a research assistant during 1959–64. He moved to [[Dynatech|Dynatech Corporation]] where he worked for a year as a staff engineer.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /> In 1965, he returned to India to join the [[Indian Institute of Technology Bombay]] as an assistant professor at the department of mechanical engineering.<ref name="INSA" /> After a series of promotions, as the professor in 1970, as the head of the department in 1973, and as the deputy director in 1975, he became the director of the institution in 1995,<ref name="IITGn" /> a post he held till he retired in 2000 with the title of the Professor Emeritus of the institution.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="Interview" /> During this period, he also had a brief stint at the [[Iowa State University]] as a visiting professor in the academic year, 1982–83. Post retirement from IIT Bombay, he worked as the chairman of the [[Atomic Energy Regulatory Board]] of the [[Government of India]] from 2000 till 2005.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IITGn" />

Suhas Sukhatme holds the life memberships of the Indian Society for Heat and Mass Transfer (ISHMT)<ref name="ISHMT">{{cite web | url=http://www.ichmt.org/index.php?Pg=InstitutionalMembers | title=ISHMT | publisher=ICHMT |year=2014 | access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref> and the Solar Energy Society of India<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="SESI">{{cite web | url=http://www.sesi.in/members.aspx | title=SESI | publisher=SESI |year=2014 | access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref> and is a former member of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] council.<ref name="INSA" /> He serves as a member of the Promotions and Assessment Committee of the [[Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore]], Nuclear Sciences Research Board of the [[Department of Atomic Energy]], and the advisory councils of the [[Indian Institute of Technology Bombay]]<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="Interview" /> and the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Gandhinagar]].
He also sits in the Governing Board of two national institutions, the [[Institute of Chemical Technology]], Mumbai and the [[National Institute of Industrial Engineering]] (NITIE), Mumbai.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" />

Sukhatme is an author of over 70 scientific papers<ref name="INSA" /> and three books viz. ''A Textbook on Heat Transfer'',<ref name="A Textbook on Heat Transfer">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-VgAZm6KWrwC | title=A Textbook on Heat Transfer | publisher=Universities Press | author=S. P. Sukhatme | year=2005 | pages=411 | isbn=9788173715440}}</ref> ''Solar Energy - Principles of Thermal Collection and Storage''<ref name="Solar Energy: Principles of Thermal Collection and Storage">{{cite book | title=Solar Energy: Principles of Thermal Collection and Storage | publisher=McGraw-Hill Education (India) | author=S. P. Sukhatme(Author), J. K. Nayak(Contributor) | date=13 January 2009 | pages=468 | isbn=978-0070142961}}</ref> and ''The Real Brain Drain''.<ref name="The Real Brain Drain">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ARsjbVvcZqkC | title=The Real Brain Drain | publisher=Orient Blackswan | author=S. P. Sukhatme | year=1994 | pages=74 | isbn=9780863114519}}</ref> His contributions are known behind the establishment of an inter-disciplinary postgraduate and research programme in Energy Systems Engineering at IIT Bombay. The program has grown over the years to become an independent department, the Department of Energy Science and Engineering.<ref name="INSA" /> He has also assisted in the formation of Mumbai-based institutions, the [[Shailesh J Mehta School of Management]] and the [[Kresit|Kanwal Rekhi School of Information Technology]].<ref name="INSA" />

Suhas Sukhatme is married to Shobha, a medical doctor and has two children, Gaurav, a member of faculty at the [[University of Southern California]] and Jai, teaching at [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]].<ref name="Interview" /> The couple lives in [[Powai]], Mumbai.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" />


==Awards and recognitions==
Sukhatme was awarded the ''Prince of Wales Gold Medal'' in 1958 by the [[Banares Hindu University]] for topping the University examinations .<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" /> In 1983, he received the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] from the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR).<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IITGn" /><ref name="SSB Prize">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=82 | title=SSB Prize | publisher=SSB Prize |year=2014 | access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref> In 2001, he received the [[Om Prakash Bhasin Award]] from Om Prakash Bhasin Foundation and the Lifetime Achievement Award from the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai]], the first recipient of the award.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IITGn" /> A recipient of the degree of the Doctor of Science (Honoris Causa) from the Banares Hindu University, Sukhatme was awarded the civilian honour of [[Padma Shri]] by the [[Government of India]] in 2001.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IITGn" />

Sukhatme delivered the Daulat Singh Kothari Memorial Award Lecture in 2005 at the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA) where he is an elected Fellow.<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" /> He is also an elected Fellow of [[Maharashtra Academy of Sciences]], [[Indian Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="Indian Academy of Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/php/fell_detail.php3?name=Sukhatme&intials=Suhas&year=05-11-1938 | title=Indian Academy of Sciences | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |year=2014 | access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref> [[Indian National Academy of Engineering]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] .<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" /><ref name="INSA" /><ref name="IITGn" /> He is an elected member of the Society of Sigma Xe and a Fellow of the [[Indian Society for Technical Education]].<ref name="ITBHU Chronicle" />
